title: Kenneth L. Gentry, Jr. et al. v. Calvary Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained. The Assembly annulled the portion of William Hyer's theological examination concerning revelation, thereby suspending Presbytery's action receiving him. Calvary Presbytery was instructed to counsel and re-examine him on that issue and report to the Fifteenth General Assembly through the Committee on Review and Control.
first_summary: Ministers challenged Calvary Presbytery's approval of William Hyer's examination and reception despite his belief in noncanonical continuing revelation. The Assembly sustained the complaint, holding those views unconstitutional, annulled his theological examination, and returned the matter for counseling and re-examination.
summary: Ministers challenged Calvary Presbytery's approval of William Hyer's examination and reception despite his belief that noncanonical, nonbinding revelation could continue. The Assembly sustained the complaint because PCA standards foreclose continuing revelation beyond illumination and providence. It annulled only the examination portion concerning revelation, suspending his reception, and instructed Presbytery to counsel and re-examine him, then report to the next Assembly. The majority deemed the record sufficient despite a dissent emphasizing Hyer's affirmation of Scripture's finality and the absence of an examination transcript.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The Assembly received and approved the Commission's statement and judgment as its own action (lines 11–15; printed pp. 224–225).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged Presbytery's sustaining Hyer's examination and receiving him despite his views on continuing revelation (lines 130–153; printed pp. 229–230).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The judgment found error, annulled only the revelation portion of the examination, suspended reception, and ordered counseling, re-examination, and reporting; the opinion held PCA standards exclude noncanonical new revelation beyond illumination and providence (lines 149–175; printed p. 230).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Tongues were not at issue. The dissent stressed Hyer's affirmations about Scripture and the incomplete examination record; the majority found the record sufficiently explicit (lines 130–140, 190–220; printed pp. 229–231).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The majority expressly concurred with the quoted doctrinal reasoning from Bogue v. Presbytery of the Ascension; this case was not disposed of merely by reference to Bogue (lines 214–220; printed p. 231).

source_limits: The dissent states that no transcript of Presbytery's detailed examination existed, although the adopted majority found the available record sufficiently explicit.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged examination and reception and the disputed continuing-revelation view.
score_reasons.decision: States the sustained complaint, limited annulment, suspended reception, and required further proceedings.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted conclusion that PCA standards prohibit the asserted category of continuing revelation.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between noncanonical revelation and illumination or providence, as well as the limited remedy.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the adopted majority judgment from the dissent and does not treat party allegations as findings.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to understand the issue, ruling, relief, and principal qualification.

verification_notes: Rechecked the Assembly's adoption, judgment, explanatory opinion, and answer to dissent. Corrected the first summary's overstatement that the entire examination was annulled: only the portion concerning revelation was annulled, reception was suspended, and counseling, re-examination, and reporting remained required.
